name: Genochondromatosis Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Hereditary Multiple Exostoses

criteria.description: Presence of multiple osteochondromas (exostoses) arising from the metaphyses of long bones
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic EXT2 gene mutation
Characteristic radiographic features including sessile or pedunculated exostoses with cartilage caps

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple osteochondromas with or without family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for EXT2 mutations can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and radiological features are typical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple osteochondromas arising from metaphyses of long bones
Cartilage-capped bony projections palpable beneath the skin
searchTerms: hard cartilage-covered bone bumps under skin

common.symptomName: Skeletal deformities including limb length discrepancies
searchTerms: bone deformities with uneven limb lengths
skeletal abnormalities causing uneven arms or legs

common.symptomName: Restricted joint motion due to exostoses impinging on adjacent structures
searchTerms: limited joint movement from bone growths
restricted motion due to bone lumps

common.symptomName: Localized pain at sites of exostoses especially after trauma
searchTerms: pain at bone growth sites especially after injury
hard lumps near joints you can feel

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms such as numbness or tingling distal to exostoses
searchTerms: numbness or tingling from nerve pressure by bone growths
tingling or loss of feeling near bone lumps

occasional.symptomName: Vascular compromise due to exostoses impinging on blood vessels
searchTerms: blood flow problems from bone pressing on vessels
vascular blockage due to bone growth

occasional.symptomName: Bursa formation overlying exostoses causing swelling
Mild limb deformities such as genu valgum or varum
searchTerms: mild leg deformities like knock-knees or bowlegs

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation of exostoses to chondrosarcoma
Respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage deformities
searchTerms: respiratory issues due to thoracic cage shape
lung compromise from chest wall abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Spinal cord compression from vertebral exostoses
searchTerms: spinal cord pressure from bone growths
nerve compression in spine due to exostoses
spinal cord symptoms from vertebral lumps

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: X-rays showing multiple sessile or pedunculated osteochondromas at metaphyses
MRI to evaluate cartilage cap thickness and potential malignant transformation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in EXT2 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Histopathology of excised lesions showing cartilage-capped bony projections

distinguishingFeatures: EXT1 gene mutation instead of EXT2
Similar clinical presentation but EXT1 mutations more common
Presence of both exostoses and enchondromas

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of exostoses suggesting malignant transformation
New onset of severe localized pain or neurological deficits
Respiratory difficulty due to thoracic cage deformities
references: Wuyts W, Van Hul W. Molecular basis of multiple exostoses: mutations in the EXT1 and EXT2 genes. Hum Mutat. 2000.
Schmale GA, Conrad EU, Raskind WH. The natural history of hereditary multiple exostoses. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1994.
